issues: Dolphin is a static, horizontal fish-like shape parked in the top third instead of a leaping/arcing creature; the entire middle band of the display is empty black.
Dolphin is far too small to be the centerpiece (occupies maybe 25% of height vs the required 50-60%), so it does not dominate.
Dolphin body is filled with flat horizontal stripes, reading as a CAD/fish drawing rather than a lit phosphor object with a rim light.
Dolphin head lacks a defined snout/beak; it reads as a generic round fish head with a single dot eye.
Bottom FFT bars are too bright and too tall, with near-white segments that out-shine the dolphin and break the visual hierarchy.
Stray star-like dots are scattered across the background, which is not part of the reference OEL aesthetic.
Large vertical gap between the high-placed dolphin and the wave lines makes the composition feel disconnected.
suggestions: Redraw the dolphin as a large, graceful leaping arc that fills the central 50-60% of the display height, with a clear snout, dorsal fin, pectoral fin, and tail fluke.
Replace the horizontal-stripe fill with a solid phosphor-lit body, a subtle rim-light edge, and a gentle bloom halo so it looks like a glowing OEL object.
Reduce FFT bar brightness and cap its height to ~13% of the display at low contrast so it stays subordinate to the dolphin.
Pull the water-surface lines up directly beneath the dolphin and keep them thin/low-contrast to close the empty gap.
Remove the random background star dots to restore the clean monochrome phosphor look.
Add short, clean persistence trails behind the dolphin to imply motion without foggy smear.
Re-balance overall brightness/contrast so the eye lands on the dolphin first, then text, waves, and FFT in that order.
